Visual-contrast path drops every non-rgb() color: bare parseRgb() silently returns null on oklch (all Tailwind v4 pages)

## Summary

Four sites in the visual-contrast path call `parseRgb()` without the `|| parseAnyColor()` fallback used everywhere else in the codebase. `parseRgb()` matches `rgba?\((\d+)...` and returns **null** for any other color space, so on a page whose computed styles are `oklch()` those checks silently receive no color and either skip or mis-score.

This affects **every Tailwind v4 project**, since v4 emits its default palette as `oklch()` and Chrome preserves that form in `getComputedStyle()` for tokenized values.

## Where, on `main` today

`cli/engine/browser/injected/index.mjs`

| Line | Call | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| 629 | `parseRgb(currentStyle.backgroundColor)` | an opaque oklch background never terminates the ancestor walk |
| 691 | `parseRgb(style.color)` | text color null → contrast check skipped |
| 988 | `parseRgb(style.backgroundColor)` | returns `unresolved: 'no readable background'` on a perfectly readable solid oklch background |
| 1118 | `parseRgb(style.color) \|\| candidate.textColor` | falls through to the inherited candidate instead of the element's own color |

Mirrored in `cli/engine/detect-antipatterns-browser.js` at 7284 / 7346 / 7643 / 7773, plus one more at **3989** (the neon-text rule), which therefore never fires on an oklch page.

The rest of the file already does the right thing — `parseRgb(x) || parseAnyColor(x)` appears at 20+ call sites, and the comment at the `parseAnyColor` definition says exactly this: *"use plain parseRgb when you only expect computed rgb() values from real browsers"*. These four are in a real-browser path where that assumption does not hold.

## Why this is not theoretical

Measuring a Tailwind v4 app, an element with `color: oklch(0.967 0.001 286.375)` on a `rgb(13,13,15)` background is a genuine **17.66:1** — but a regex that reads the three oklch components as r/g/b computes **2.67:1** and reports a false failure. I hit exactly this with my own ad-hoc checker before finding that this repo already had the correct resolver. The inverse also happens: a real failure scores as a pass and is never reported.

## `parseAnyColor` is already exact — no canvas needed

I considered proposing a canvas round-trip (`fillStyle` + `getImageData`), which resolves any CSS color exactly as the browser does. It is unnecessary: I compared this repo's `oklchToRgb` / `oklabToRgb` against `canvas` ground truth in Chrome across the gamut.

| Input | `oklchToRgb` | canvas | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| `oklch(0.967 0.001 286.375)` | 244,244,245 | 244,244,245 | 0 |
| `oklch(84% 0.19 80.46)` | 255,186,0 | 255,186,0 | 0 |
| `oklch(0.5 0.2 250)` | 0,97,206 | 0,97,206 | 0 |
| `oklch(0.65 0.28 20)` (out of gamut) | 255,0,64 | 255,0,64 | 0 |
| `oklch(0.9 0.15 140)` | 167,246,149 | 167,246,149 | 0 |
| `oklch(0.145 0 0)` | 10,10,10 | 10,10,10 | 0 |
| `oklch(1 0 0)` | 255,255,255 | 255,255,255 | 0 |
| `oklch(0.7 0.1 200deg)` | — | — | 0 |

**Worst delta across 10 cases: 0**, including gamut clamping and `deg` units.

Canvas would also be wrong architecturally here: the static-html engine runs on jsdom, which has no canvas, so it would only work in one of the engines while `parseAnyColor` works in all of them.

## Proposed fix

One token per site, matching the existing convention:

```diff
-      const solidBg = parseRgb(currentStyle.backgroundColor);
+      const solidBg = parseRgb(currentStyle.backgroundColor) || parseAnyColor(currentStyle.backgroundColor);
```

…and the same at 691, 988, 1118, plus the bundle twins and 3989.

I've applied this locally against 4.0.4 and both artifacts pass `node --check`. Happy to open a PR if useful — say the word and I'll send it against `main`.

## Not verified

I have not run a before/after detector pass to quantify the change in finding counts; the target page is behind auth in my environment. The defect and the resolver equivalence are both verified directly, but the downstream effect on reported findings is inferred.

detect.mjs silently drops root-relative linked stylesheets, hiding every contrast finding

## Summary

`collectStaticCssText` resolves `<link rel="stylesheet">` hrefs with `path.resolve(fileDir, href)`. When the href is **root-relative** (`/static/app.css`), `path.resolve` discards `fileDir` entirely — the path is already absolute — so it looks for the sheet at the filesystem root. The read fails and is swallowed by `catch { /* skip unreadable */ }`.

The result: the entire stylesheet is invisible to the static-HTML engine, no warning is printed, and **every rule that depends on resolved custom properties or computed colour silently reports nothing.**

This is not platform-specific. `path.resolve('/project/public', '/static/app.css')` returns `/static/app.css` on POSIX and `C:\static\app.css` on Windows. Both are wrong; both fail quietly.

## Reproduction

A page that links its stylesheet root-relative, as a site served from a web root normally would:

```html
<!-- public/index.html -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/static/tool-shell.css">
```

```
node scripts/detect.mjs --json public/index.html
```

Measured on a real page in our repo (~4,300 lines, one root-relative sheet carrying all design tokens):

| | findings | `low-contrast` |
|---|---|---|
| as the page links it (`/static/…`) | **28** | **0** |
| identical page, href rewritten to `static/…`, sheet copied alongside | **46** | **16** |

18 findings invisible, including every contrast finding. The 16 `low-contrast` results are real — they name a genuine 3.98:1 pairing we have a documented waiver for.

## Why it is worth fixing rather than documenting

The `DEGRADED` banner already exists for the case where the parser modules are unavailable, and it is genuinely useful — it tells you the run is an undercount. This failure mode produces the same undercount with **no** signal, so a clean-looking `0 contrast findings` reads as a pass.

We acted on three critique rounds against this page before noticing. Each one reported detector output as evidence; each was reading roughly 60% of the stylesheet-dependent rules.

## Suggested fix

Two parts, either useful alone:

1. **Resolve root-relative hrefs against a document root.** A reasonable default is the nearest ancestor directory of the scanned file containing `index.html`, or an explicit `--root` flag. Falling back to `fileDir` when nothing is found keeps current behaviour for relative hrefs.

2. **Warn instead of swallowing.** `catch { /* skip unreadable */ }` could emit the same class of notice the parser-module path does — e.g. `impeccable detect: could not read linked stylesheet <href> (resolved to <path>); colour and custom-property rules will be incomplete`. That alone would have surfaced this immediately.

The comment directly above the `path.resolve` call shows the cache-busting case (`styles.css?v=3`) was considered carefully — a leading slash is the same class of problem and currently has the same consequence the comment describes: "the whole stylesheet invisible to every element-level check".

## Environment

- impeccable skill v4.1.1 (`npx impeccable install`, global)
- Node 24 on Windows 11
- `scripts/detector/engines/static-html/css-cascade.mjs`, the `collectStaticCssText` loop (~line 980 in this build)

Happy to send a PR if the document-root approach is the direction you'd want.

[security] detect leaks embedded basic-auth credentials verbatim into finding output (text and --json)

Scanning a URL with HTTP Basic Auth embedded (`impeccable detect https://user:password@host.com`) causes the plaintext credential to appear, unredacted, in every finding produced by that scan, in both plain-text and `--json` output.

**Root cause:**
- `cli/engine/engines/browser/detect-url.mjs`: the scan function returns `results.map(f => finding(f.id, url, f.snippet))`, where `url` is the literal CLI argument.
- `cli/engine/findings.mjs`: `finding(id, filePath, snippet, line)` stores that string unmodified as `file`, no check for userinfo, no redaction.
- `cli/engine/cli/main.mjs`: prints `file` verbatim in text mode, and `JSON.stringify`s the full findings array (including `file`) for `--json`.

**Why this matters more than it might look:** there's no alternative auth mechanism today, no `--header`, no `--auth-user`/`--auth-pass`, no cookie support, and the Puppeteer instance never calls `page.authenticate()`. Credential-in-URL is the only way to scan a protected page right now, and it's also the only path that leaks it. A scan result is often piped into logs, CI artifacts, or handed to an AI coding agent as part of a normal workflow, all of which can durably persist or redisplay it well past the original scan.

Worth noting the exposure isn't limited to classic basic-auth syntax either: since nothing sanitizes any part of the scan-target URL, the same leak would happen with any other credential-bearing URL, for example a presigned URL with a signature in the query string, or a link carrying an API key or access token as a query parameter.

**Suggested fix:** use Puppeteer's `page.authenticate({username, password})` to handle basic auth instead of relying on URL-embedded credentials, and store/print a credential-stripped version of the URL as `file` regardless.

**Repro:**
```
npx impeccable detect https://user:pass@example.com --json
```
Every finding's `file` field will contain the literal credential.

[Bug] Firefox 1.4.0 release artifact cannot scan and release does not warn about it

## What happened?

I installed the Firefox build from the latest extension release, `ext-v1.4.0`, using the provided `extension-firefox.zip`.

When trying to scan a page, Impeccable fails to start the rule core with:

```text
Couldn’t start the rule core: Type error for parameter filter (Error processing contextTypes.0: Invalid enumeration value "OFFSCREEN_DOCUMENT") for runtime.getContexts.
```

This happens because the 1.4.0 extension calls:

```js
chrome.runtime.getContexts({
  contextTypes: ['OFFSCREEN_DOCUMENT'],
  ...
});
```

and then relies on `chrome.offscreen.createDocument(...)`. Firefox does not support Chrome's offscreen document API.

What makes this especially confusing is that the release itself provides a file named `extension-firefox.zip` without any warning in the release notes that scanning is currently unsupported on Firefox.

The repository already documents the limitation internally in `scripts/build-extension.js`:

> Firefox caveat: the shell runs the WebAssembly rule core in an extension offscreen document, and Gecko has no `chrome.offscreen` API, so the Firefox package builds and lints but cannot scan until that gap is closed.

The build script also prints:

> Warning: the Firefox package cannot scan yet.

So the incompatibility appears to be known, but that information is not visible when a user finds the latest Firefox artifact from the Releases page.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the `ext-v1.4.0` GitHub release.
2. Download and install `extension-firefox.zip` in Firefox.
3. Open a normal web page and run an Impeccable scan.
4. Observe the rule-core startup error about `OFFSCREEN_DOCUMENT`.

## Expected behavior

Ideally, the Firefox build should support scanning.

Until Firefox support for the 1.4 architecture exists, the GitHub release should clearly state that `extension-firefox.zip` is not currently functional for scanning, or the artifact should not be presented as a normal usable Firefox release.

### What is the problem you are having with rclone?

When container soft delete is enabled on a storage account, rclone lists the soft deleted containers at the root of the account as if they were normal containers.

`rclone lsd remote:` shows them. `rclone sync remote: dest` then fails to list each of them with `directory not found`. Because of these errors, sync refuses to delete anything on the destination (`not deleting files as there were IO errors`), and it ends with exit code 3.

We hit this on a real backup: a nightly `rclone sync` between two storage accounts, at the account root. About 300 containers are deleted each month on the source, so every run fails and no deletion is ever propagated.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Create a storage account with container soft delete enabled (any retention).
2. Create two containers, `keep` and `gone`, with one small file in each.
3. Delete `gone`. Azure keeps it as soft deleted.
4. Run `rclone lsd remote:`: `gone` is listed.

drive: ListR (--fast-list) deadlocks when a listing error arrives while directories are in the overflow queue (send on nil channel under mu)

### Before you start

- [x] I have searched the forum and the existing issues for this problem. The closest are #9416 (a different deadlock, in `fs/walk/walk.go:436`) and PR #9811 (rewrites `listRRunner` but does not touch the block below).
- [ ] I have tested with the latest beta or stable release and can still reproduce the problem. Three v1.73.2 runs wedged the same way within 12 hours; the third is captured in the goroutine dump below. I have not re-run it on v1.75.2, but the code involved is byte-identical in v1.75.2 and on master (`backend/drive/drive.go` lines 2297 to 2333 there).
- [x] This is a reproducible bug, not a usage question.

### What is the problem you are having with rclone?

`rclone sync` with `--fast-list` against Google Drive hangs forever during the listing. CPU stops, no I/O, no log lines except the `--stats` block, and `--timeout` / `--max-duration` never fire. A goroutine dump (via `--rc` `debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=2`) shows a deadlock inside `backend/drive` `(*Fs).ListR`, between the overflow goroutine and the main error loop.

Line numbers below are v1.73.2 `backend/drive/drive.go`:

```go
2224	mu := sync.Mutex{} // protects in and overflow
...
2269	go func() {
2270		// wait until the all directories are processed
2271		wg.Wait()
2272		// if the input channel overflowed add the collected entries to the channel now
2273		for len(overflow) > 0 {
2274			mu.Lock()
2275			// only fill half of the channel to prevent entries being put into overflow again
2276			l := min(len(overflow), listRInputBuffer/2)
2277			wg.Add(l)
2278			for _, d := range overflow[:l] {
2279				in <- d
2280			}
2281			overflow = overflow[l:]
2282			mu.Unlock()
...
2295	// wait until the all workers to finish
2296	for range f.ci.Checkers {
2297		e := <-out
2298		mu.Lock()
2299		// if one worker returns an error early, close the input so all other workers exit
2300		if e != nil && in != nil {
2301			err = e
2302			close(in)
2303			in = nil
2304		}
2305		mu.Unlock()
2306	}
```

Sequence:

1. The tree has more pending directories than `listRInputBuffer` (1000), so `sendJob` puts some into `overflow`.
2. A `listRRunner` worker returns an error (here a 403 `rateLimitExceeded` from the Drive API). The main loop takes `mu`, closes `in` and sets `in = nil` (2302 to 2303).
3. The remaining workers exit, `wg` reaches zero, and the overflow goroutine wakes at 2271. `overflow` is not empty, so it takes `mu` (2274) and sends on `in` (2279). `in` is now `nil`, so the send blocks forever, while holding `mu`.
4. The main loop receives the next worker's result from `out` and blocks on `mu.Lock()` at 2298 forever. `ListR` never returns, so the error is never logged and the sync never retries or exits.

If the main loop drains all of `out` before step 3, `ListR` returns the error normally but the overflow goroutine is leaked, still blocked on the nil channel (and holding that call's `mu`). The dump below shows both outcomes in one process: the leak from the first sync attempt and the deadlock from the second.

Conditions: `--fast-list`, a tree with more than 1000 directories pending at once (ours has about 51,000 directories, 300,000 entries), and any worker error during the listing. With rclone's shared client_id the 403 rate-limit errors are frequent: 3 of 5 runs in 12 hours wedged in the listing (only the last one was dumped).

Possible fix: stop feeding the overflow once the listing has been aborted, for example

```go
for len(overflow) > 0 {
	mu.Lock()
	if in == nil {
		// listing aborted by an error: workers are gone, drop the overflow
		overflow = nil
		mu.Unlock()
		break
	}
	...
```

(or select on a done channel instead of sending on `in` directly).

ftp: connections that fail with network errors are returned to the pool, causing permanent failure of sequential operations

### Before you start

- [x] I have searched the [forum](https://forum.rclone.org/) and the existing issues for this problem.
- [x] I have tested with the latest beta or stable release and can still reproduce the problem.
- [x] This is a reproducible bug, not a usage question (questions belong on the forum).

### Associated forum post URL

_No response_

### What is the problem you are having with rclone?

Disclaimer: This issue describes a real-world production scenario (restic backups against a rate limited FTP server) that I experienced myself. The root-cause analysis, the suggested fix, and the wording of this report were produced with help of an LLM. The result of the patch was verified by me against the described setup.

When an FTP operation fails with a raw network error (server closed/RST an idle control connection: `wsasend: An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host`, `unexpected EOF`, ...), `putFtpConnection()` puts the dead connection back into the pool without any liveness check, and `getFtpConnection()` hands it straight
back out. Sequential operations can therefore fail indefinitely: each attempt picks the dead pool-head connection, fails, and re-pools it. Parallel operations appear to "self-heal" (concurrent callers momentarily empty the pool and force fresh dials), which makes the bug look intermittent and server-side.

Verified still present in v1.75.2 and current master (`backend/ftp/ftp.go`,
`putFtpConnection`):

```go
if err != nil {
    // If not a regular FTP error code then check the connection
    if tpErr := textprotoError(err); tpErr != nil {   // <-- only *textproto.Error
        nopErr := c.NoOp()
        if nopErr != nil {
            fs.Debugf(f, "Connection failed, closing: %v", nopErr)
            _ = c.Quit()
            return
        }
    }
}
f.poolMu.Lock()
f.pool = append(f.pool, c)   // <-- network errors (tpErr == nil) land here
```

`textprotoError()` matches only `*textproto.Error` (real FTP reply codes), so a connection that just failed with `ECONNRESET`/EOF skips the NOOP probe and is pooled as if healthy. Note the comment says the opposite of what the code does: it checks the connection only *for* regular FTP error codes, not when the error is *not* one.

`--ftp-idle-timeout` doesn't help: `f.drain` is a single global timer reset on every `putFtpConnection()`, so under any ongoing pool activity individually dead connections are never drained.

### Reproduction

1. `rclone serve restic --addr :18000 ftp:test --ftp-concurrency 4 --log-level DEBUG`
2.  Generate load that leaves 2–3 of the 4 pooled connections idle past the server's idle timeout while one stays busy (e.g. a long download in a loop).
3. Kill the idle server-side connections (`ss -K`, firewall RST, or wait out the timeout).
4. Run a **sequential** operation (single `rclone size` / one small PUT in a loop): it fails with `wsasend`/EOF on every attempt while the concurrent transfer keeps working. The debug log shows no `Connection failed, closing` line — the dead connection is silently re-pooled.

### Expected behavior

A connection that failed with a non-protocol (network) error is never returned to the pool — it is closed and discarded.

### Suggested fix

```go
if err != nil {
    // Any error that is not a plain FTP reply code means we can no longer
    // trust the control connection - discard it.
    if tpErr := textprotoError(err); tpErr == nil {
        _ = c.Quit()
        return
    }
    if nopErr := c.NoOp(); nopErr != nil {
        fs.Debugf(f, "Connection failed, closing: %v", nopErr)
        _ = c.Quit()
        return
    }
}
```

Optionally additionally: per-connection staleness (track `lastUsed`, evict at `getFtpConnection()` time if older than `IdleTimeout`), or a NOOP probe on checkout after a period of idleness.

I've implemented and verified both changes (discard on network error + NOOP probe on checkout when idle > 10 s) against a local `rclone serve ftp` that is `kill -9`ed and restarted while `rclone serve restic` holds pooled connections: unpatched fails permanently (14 pool errors, timeout); patched recovers transparently, exit 0.

### Before you start

- [x] I have searched the [forum](https://forum.rclone.org/) and the existing issues for this problem.

### What is the problem you are having with rclone?

When `rclone serve restic` receives a `DELETE` request and the lookup of the object fails with an error other than "not found", it replies `404 Not Found`. A `GET` request with the same lookup error replies `500 Internal Server Error`.

restic treats a 404 on delete as final and does not retry. When this happens while restic removes its lock, the lock stays in the repository and the next exclusive operation (for example `forget --prune`) fails with "repository is already locked". The real error is logged only at debug level.

We hit this in production with a Backblaze B2 remote: a temporary error from B2 while restic removed its lock made the following `forget --prune` fail. The steps below use a local remote and a permission error, to get the same lookup failure deterministically.

In `cmd/serve/restic/restic.go`, `deleteObject()` replies 404 for any error returned by `s.newObject()`, while `serveObject()` replies 404 only for `fs.ErrorObjectNotFound` and 500 otherwise. Replying 500 for other errors in `deleteObject()` too would let restic retry.

**Steps to reproduce** (run as root with Podman; rclone runs as uid 1000, so an unreadable `locks` directory gives a lookup error that is not "not found"):

```bash
D=/tmp/rclone-repro; URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080/repo
mkdir -p $D/data && chown -R 1000:1000 $D
podman run -d --name rclone-repro --user 1000:1000 --network host -v $D/data:/data:Z \
    docker.io/rclone/rclone:1.75.2 serve restic --addr 127.0.0.1:8080 --cache-objects=false -vv /data
restic() { podman run --rm -i --network host -e RESTIC_REPOSITORY=rest:$URL -e RESTIC_PASSWORD=test \
    docker.io/restic/restic:0.19.1 "$@"; }
restic init -q

# 1. Same lookup error: GET replies 500, DELETE replies 404
id=$(printf 'a%.0s' {1..64})
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "POST %{http_code}\n" --data-binary test -X POST $URL/locks/$id
chmod 000 $D/data/repo/locks
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "GET %{http_code}\n" $URL/locks/$id
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "DELETE %{http_code}\n" -X DELETE $URL/locks/$id
chmod 755 $D/data/repo/locks; ls $D/data/repo/locks; rm $D/data/repo/locks/$id

# 2. restic loses its lock: make locks/ unreadable while a backup runs
( sleep 10; echo hello ) | restic backup -q --stdin --stdin-filename hello.txt &
sleep 5; chmod 000 $D/data/repo/locks; wait; chmod 755 $D/data/repo/locks
restic list locks
restic forget -q --keep-last 1 --prune
```

```
GET 500
```

### What is the problem you are having with rclone?

Uploading many files to a WebDAV remote running OpenCloud (ownCloud Infinite
Scale, configured with vendor `owncloud-infinite-scale`) makes rclone's memory
usage grow by roughly the size of every uploaded file. The growth is strictly
linear with the number of files copied and never shrinks, so after a few
thousand files the process consumes several GB and is killed by the kernel's
OOM killer. The transfers themselves all succeed; the only symptom is the
memory growth.

### rclone version

### Operating system

Linux

### Which cloud storage system are you using?

Source: `seafile` backend (Seafile server), Destination: `webdav` backend with vendor `owncloud-infinite-scale`   (OpenCloud server)  The destination backend is the relevant one. The seafile side was checked and is not involved.

### Output of `rclone config redacted`

```ini
vendor = infinitescale

pass = XXX

```

### The command you were trying to run

```shell
GOGC=20 rclone copyto -P -c --multi-thread-streams 2 --max-backlog 1000 --max-buffer-memory 500M  --max-connections 2  "SeafileUser:Downloads" "Opencloud:User/Downloads/"
```

### A log from the command with the `-vv` flag

```shell
The log is fine, when there are not too many files, everything works fine.
```

### Anything else?

Run the copy with `--rc --rc-no-auth` and, while it runs, fetch the goroutine
profile:

```console
curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:5572/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=1' | grep -c broadcastProgress
```

The number of goroutines parked in `webdav.(*Uploader).broadcastProgress`
equals the number of files copied so far and grows by one per file.
Alternatively run rclone with stderr captured and send `kill -QUIT <pid>`;
the goroutine dump written to stderr shows the same picture.

Every upload to the `infinitescale` vendor goes through the tus protocol
implementation in `backend/webdav/tus-upload.go` and `tus-uploader.go`:

1. `tus-uploader.go` `NewUploader()` starts `go uploader.broadcastProgress()`.
   `broadcastProgress()` waits forever on `for range u.notifyChan`, and
   nothing in the code ever closes `u.notifyChan`, so exactly one goroutine
   per uploaded file stays blocked forever.
2. A goroutine blocked on a channel keeps every value it references alive, so
   that goroutine pins the `Uploader` and its `*Upload`.
3. `tus-upload.go` `NewUpload()` buffers the entire file into a `bytes.Buffer`
   because the reader that `fs/operations` hands to `Update()`
   (`tr.Account(...).WithBuffer()`) is not an `io.ReadSeeker`, and the tus
   uploader `Seek`s in the stream for its chunked PATCH uploads.

Together this retains a full in-memory copy of every file ever uploaded plus
one goroutine each. A unit test against a local fake tus server reproduces
this on v1.75.2 and current master:

- 10 files x 1 MiB -> 10 leaked goroutines, ~20 MiB still on the heap after a
  forced GC
- 30 files x 1 MiB -> 30 leaked goroutines, ~60 MiB
- 60 files x 1 MiB -> 60 leaked goroutines, ~120 MiB

(The ~2x factor comes from `bytes.Buffer` capacity over-allocation.)

This also means the peak memory for uploading a single large file through
this path is unbounded, since the whole file is buffered in RAM before the
first byte is sent.

### Suggested fix

Make the progress broadcasting goroutine exit when the upload is finished by
closing the notification channel when `Uploader.Upload()` returns:

```go
func (u *Uploader) Upload(ctx context.Context, options ...fs.OpenOption) error {
	defer close(u.notifyChan)
	...
}
```

ftp: early-closed RETR answered with 425 puts a QUIT connection back in the pool (serve s3 ranged GET fails)

#### What is the problem you are having with rclone?

`rclone serve s3` (VFS, `--vfs-cache-mode off`) on top of an FTPES remote (Egnyte) fails on ranged GETs under light parallel load. The client gets `500 InternalError`, sometimes `NoSuchBucket`, and the server log shows `425 "Can't open data connection."` followed by repeated `use of closed network connection`.

What we see in the code and logs (v1.75.2):

1. A ranged read through the VFS first opens the object at offset 0 (`openPending` → `chunkedreader.Open`), then seeks, so `openRange` opens a second `REST <off>` + `RETR` and only then closes the first one.
2. The first `RETR` is closed before anything is read. jlaffaye/ftp does not send `ABOR`; Egnyte answers the close with `425` (sometimes `426`).
3. `ftpReadCloser.Close` treats 425 as an error: it runs `Quit()` and `putFtpConnection(nil, nil)`, but keeps `f.c`. 425 is not in the masked codes (426, 550, 150, 250).
4. `resetReader` returns the error before replacing the reader, so the VFS retries and closes the same `ftpReadCloser` again. The second `Response.Close()` returns nil, so `putFtpConnection(&f.c, nil)` puts the QUIT connection into the pool and returns the token a second time.
5. Later operations take the dead connection; `use of closed network connection` is retried on it until low-level retries run out.

The beta with #10102 (`ebfaae73c9`) helps (dead connections are dropped), but each incident still costs retries: 1 GB download in ~500 s with 134 `use of closed` lines, against ~77–300 s and 0 errors with the patch below.

#### What is your rclone version (output from `rclone version`)

rclone v1.75.2 (also checked v1.76.0-beta.10625.545b142ad)

#### Which OS you are using and how many bits (e.g. Windows 7, 64 bit)

linux/amd64 (Docker, rclone/rclone:1.75.2) and darwin/arm64

#### Which cloud storage system are you using? (e.g. Google Drive)

FTP with explicit TLS (Egnyte, `ftp-<domain>.egnyte.com`)

#### The command you were trying to run (e.g. `rclone copy /tmp remote:tmp`)

```
rclone serve s3 egnyte:/Shared/S3 --vfs-cache-mode off --addr :8080 --auth-key KEY,SECRET
# remote: type=ftp, explicit_tls=true, no_check_upload=true, concurrency=6
aws s3 cp s3://bucket/big-1g.bin ./big-1g.bin   # classic transfer client, 4 parallel 16 MiB ranges
```

#### A log from the command with the `-vv` flag

```
DEBUG : FTP Tx: "REST 8388608"
DEBUG : FTP Rx: "350 Restarting at 8388608. Send STORE or RETRIEVE to initiate transfer."
DEBUG : FTP Tx: "RETR /Shared/S3/bucket/big-1g.bin"
DEBUG : FTP Rx: "150 File status okay; about to open data connection."
ERROR : bucket/big-1g.bin: ReadFileHandle.Read error: low level retry 1/10: 1 error occurred:
	* 425 "Can't open data connection."
DEBUG : pacer: low level retry 1/10 (error use of closed network connection)
...
DEBUG : pacer: low level retry 10/10 (error use of closed network connection)
ERROR : serve s3: open: use of closed network connection
```

#### Proposed fix

In `backend/ftp/ftp.go` `ftpReadCloser`:

- a `closed` flag so a second `Close` does nothing (no pool put, no second token);
- `f.c = nil` after `Quit()`;
- count bytes returned by `Read` and mask `425` only when nothing was read (a transfer cut after data stays an error).

With this patch on top of v1.75.2 + `ebfaae73c9`: 3/3 downloads of 1 GB with matching sha256, 0 errors, at most 6 FTP sessions; restic 10 GB backup, `check --read-data` and restore green. Happy to open a PR with unit tests (double `Close`, 425 with 0 and >0 bytes read).

Related, not fixed by this: `openRange` opens the new `RETR` before closing the old one, so with `concurrency=N` and N parallel reads every reader holds one token and waits for a second (`TokenDispenser.Get` has no context), which can hang `serve s3`.

### What problem are you trying to solve?

When verifying a checksum manifest against the local backend, `rclone checksum` appears to hash only one file at a time unless `--download` is specified.

For example:

```sh
rclone checksum sha256 manifest.txt . --one-way --progress
```

uses the normal backend `Hash()` path, but in rclone v1.75.0 that path is handled synchronously inside `operations.CheckSum()`.

Adding:

```sh
--download
```

causes the file-content hashing to run concurrently, limited by `--checkers`.

This is unintuitive for the local backend. In both cases, rclone ultimately needs to read and hash local file contents, but concurrency is only enabled when `--download` is used.

It also means `rclone checksum` can be substantially slower than necessary on fast local storage.

The same behavior affects:

```sh
rclone check manifest.txt . --checkfile sha256
```

because it uses the same `operations.CheckSum()` implementation.

### How do you think rclone should be changed to solve that?

Please make the non-`--download` path in `operations.CheckSum()` perform `obj.Hash()` calls concurrently, limited by `--checkers`.

Currently, the non-download branch calls `obj.Hash()` synchronously, while the download branch already uses goroutines and the existing checker token pool.

Ideally:

```sh
rclone checksum sha256 manifest.txt . --checkers 8
```

would perform up to eight backend hash operations concurrently without requiring:

```sh
--download
```

This would make the behavior more consistent with the meaning of `--checkers`, improve local checksum verification performance, and also benefit `rclone check --checkfile`.

### What is the problem you are having with rclone?

`rclone copy` panics with a nil pointer dereference partway through an ~85GB
multipart upload to an S3-compatible backend (MinIO, fronted by a MinIO
`sidekick` load balancer). The panic is not from a network error — it happens
*after* `UploadPart` returns successfully (no error from the pacer), while
logging the result.

Root cause (traced against the v1.75.0 tag):

`backend/s3/s3.go`, in `s3ChunkWriter.WriteChunk`:

    w.addCompletedPart(s3PartNumber, uout.ETag)          // line 4666 — fine, doesn't deref
    fs.Debugf(w.o, "multipart upload wrote chunk %d with %v bytes and etag %v",
        chunkNumber+1, currentChunkSize, *uout.ETag)       // line 4668 — unconditional deref

If the backend answers a given `UploadPart` request with HTTP success but an
empty/absent `ETag` header, `uout.ETag` is `nil`, `err` is `nil` (so the pacer
loop doesn't retry), and the very next line panics dereferencing it — purely
for a debug log message, not for anything load-bearing. This is inconsistent
with how the same file handles a possibly-nil `ETag` elsewhere, e.g.
`uploadSinglepartPutObject` guards it via `stringClone(deref(resp.ETag))`.

Whether the backend *should* ever omit `ETag` on a 200 is a separate
question (still being investigated on our infra side — MinIO/proxy issue
under load), but rclone crashing the whole transfer on it, from a log
statement, is a bug regardless.

Suggested fix: nil-guard the log line (or better, treat a nil `ETag` on a
successful response as a retryable/error condition inside the pacer
callback, since silently completing a part with no ETag is itself
questionable).

rc core/bwlimit: sub-KiB rate is scaled by 1024 when the reported rate is fed back in

#### What is the problem you are having with rclone?

`BwPair.String()` prints a sub-KiB bandwidth without a unit, and `Set` reads a bare number as KiB, so a bandwidth below 1 KiB is multiplied by 1024 when it goes through a string.

This is the same corruption as 63c4fef27 ("fs: fix corruption of SizeSuffix with `B` suffix in config"), which fixed it for `fs.Option` by suffixing bare numbers with `B`. `BwPair.String()` calls `SizeSuffix.String()` directly, so it never got that treatment.

It shows up on `rc core/bwlimit`, which documents that the returned `rate` uses the same format as the `rate` parameter and as `--bwlimit`:

```
rclone rc core/bwlimit rate=500B
{
    "bytesPerSecond": 500,
    "rate": "500"
}
```

Feeding that `rate` back in gives a limit 1024 times larger:

```
rclone rc core/bwlimit rate=500
{
    "bytesPerSecond": 512000,
    "rate": "500Ki"
}
```

So anything that reads the current limit and writes it back, or restores a saved value, silently raises the limit.

#### What is your rclone version?

master at 4e7a21bea

#### Which OS you are using and how many bits

macOS 15.1, darwin/arm64

#### How to replicate with a test

```go
var tt fs.BwTimetable
tt.Set("500B")          // Tx: 500
printed := tt.String()  // "500"

var got fs.BwTimetable
got.Set(printed)        // Tx: 512000
```

The same holds for `1B`, `1023B`, `1B:2B` and `Mon-10:00,500B`. Values of 1 KiB and above already round trip, because their suffix is not a digit.

I have a fix that moves the `B` suffixing out of `Option.String()` into a `SizeSuffix` method and uses it from `BwPair.String()` too, with a round trip test. Happy to open a PR.

[Bug] Antigravity 400 on /v1/responses: 'function call turn comes immediately after a user turn...' (gemini models, reasoning+function_call history)

## Environment
- CLIProxyAPI version: **v7.2.131** (Commit: `323b7276`, BuiltAt: 2026-08-13T06:40:28Z)
- Platform: Linux amd64
- Endpoint: `POST /v1/responses`

## Problem
When using **gemini models** (e.g. `gemini-3.7-flash-high`, `gemini-3.6-flash-high`) through the Responses API in a **multi-turn conversation that includes function calls**, the request fails with HTTP 400 from the Antigravity upstream:

```json
{"error":{"code":"400","message":"Please ensure that function call turn comes immediately after a user turn or after a function response turn."}}
```

Upstream URL: `https://daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com/v1internal:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse` (provider=antigravity)

Trace ID: `20260814125658-73e52601fc5854d7`

## Reproduction

The failing request's `input` looks like this (note the `reasoning` item immediately before `function_call`):

```json
{
  "model": "gemini-3.7-flash-high",
  "input": [
    {"type": "reasoning", "id": "rs_resp_..._detached_before_0", "summary": [], "encrypted_content": "cpa-gemini-responses-carrier-v1:next:function:..."},
    {"type": "function_call", "call_id": "call_...", "name": "Bash", "arguments": "{...}"},
    {"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": "call_...", "output": "..."},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "..."}]},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "..."}]}
  ]
}
```

The client sends `reasoning` (carrier) + `function_call` consecutively. After CLIProxyAPI converts this to the native Antigravity/Gemini format, the `reasoning` turn becomes a "model turn", and the following `function_call` violates the upstream constraint that a function-call turn must come immediately after a **user turn** or a **function response turn**.

## What works

- Same sequence with **claude models** (`claude-sonnet-4-6`) → ✅ works
- `user → function_call → function_call_output → user` → ✅ works
- Plain multi-turn chat without function calls → ✅ works
- Single turn → ✅ works
- Only fails when `reasoning` item appears right before `function_call` in the history

## Expected
- `reasoning` items (especially the `cpa-gemini-responses-carrier-v1:next:function:*` carrier) should be dropped or reordered so the converted Antigravity turn sequence stays valid (function_call after user/function_response), e.g. merging/removing the reasoning turn when it precedes a function_call.

## Notes
- Impact: any client doing long agentic (tool-calling) sessions on gemini models hits this after a few rounds.
- Workaround: use claude models or start a fresh conversation.

[Bug/Architecture] Antigravity consumer accounts must exclusively use daily-cloudcode-pa to prevent 429 cooldown cascades

## 📌 Problem & Symptom

In CLIProxyAPI (CPA), Antigravity OAuth accounts (Google AI Pro, Ultra, One, and Free tier) frequently encounter cascading `429 Too Many Requests / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` errors, which causes CPA to mark healthy credentials as unavailable and place them into **Cooldown**. Over time, this leads to large-scale account pool starvation.

---

## 🔬 Root Cause Analysis

We investigated this through both **binary disassembly of the official `agy` client (`~/.local/bin/agy`)** and **live API probing across 24 active consumer accounts**.

### 1. Official `agy` Routing Architecture
In `codeassistclient.(*CLIAuthProvider).ResolveAuthMode` and `UpdateEndpointURL`:
1. `agy` queries `POST /v1internal:loadCodeAssist` to determine user entitlements.
2. For personal Google accounts (Free, Pro, Ultra, Google One where `gcpManaged == false`), it resolves to `AuthMode: personal_consumer`.
3. In `UpdateEndpointURL`, `personal_consumer` accounts are **strictly and exclusively bound to `https://daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com`**.
4. **Zero Cross-Tier Fallback:** The official `agy` client **never** falls back to `cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com` for consumer accounts. The two backends are strictly partitioned.

### 2. Live Probe Verification (24 Active Accounts)
Using identical request payloads, headers, and OAuth access tokens:
* `https://daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com`: **100% (24/24) return HTTP 200 OK** with smooth streaming generation.
* `https://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com`: **100% (24/24) return HTTP 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED** because Google gates this endpoint to enterprise/GCP-licensed accounts.

### 3. The Fallback Cascading Cooldown Trap in CPA
Currently, in `internal/runtime/executor/antigravity_executor_request.go`:
```go
var antigravityBaseURLFallbackOrder = func(auth *cliproxyauth.Auth) []string {
    if base := resolveCustomAntigravityBaseURL(auth); base != "" {
        return []string{base}
    }
    return []string{
        antigravityBaseURLDaily,
        antigravityBaseURLProd, // https://cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com
    }
}
```
1. When a consumer account experiences transient latency or single-request concurrency throttling on `daily`, CPA retries against `prod` (`cloudcode-pa`).
2. `cloudcode-pa` **always answers 429** for consumer accounts.
3. CPA interprets this as genuine quota exhaustion and puts the healthy credential into **Cooldown**.
4. Traffic rolls over to the next credential, triggering the same failure loop until the entire account pool is locked out.

---

## 🎯 Proposed Fix

### 1. Remove `cloudcode-pa` from Default Fallback
In `internal/runtime/executor/antigravity_executor_request.go`, restrict the default slice to `antigravityBaseURLDaily` only:

```diff
--- a/internal/runtime/executor/antigravity_executor_request.go
+++ b/internal/runtime/executor/antigravity_executor_request.go
@@ -439,7 +439,6 @@ var antigravityBaseURLFallbackOrder = func(auth *cliproxyauth.Auth) []string {
 	}
 	return []string{
 		antigravityBaseURLDaily,
-		antigravityBaseURLProd,
 		// antigravitySandboxBaseURLDaily,
 	}
 }
```

*(Note: Custom endpoints can still be explicitly configured per-credential via `base_url` in auth JSON / attributes).*

---

## 📋 Additional Observation: Quota RPC
Official `agy` defines `POST /v1internal:retrieveUserQuotaSummary` (`RetrieveUserQuotaResponse` with `BucketInfo` containing `remaining_fraction`, `remaining_amount`, and `reset_time`), which can be leveraged for proactive quota accounting and intelligent credential scheduling in the future.

fix(translator): hoisting mid-session developer messages to systemInstruction breaks Gemini prompt caching

## Summary

When proxying OpenAI Responses API requests to Google Gemini / Antigravity, mid-session `developer` role messages (such as `<image_resize_notice>`, `<permissions instructions>`, or `<collaboration_mode>` frequently emitted by Codex Desktop and Codex CLI) are hoisted out of `input` and appended to the top-level `systemInstruction`.

Because Google Gemini's context caching (Paged KV Checkpoint) relies on strict prefix matching starting from `systemInstruction` at Token 0, mutating `systemInstruction` mid-session completely invalidates the accumulated prefix cache for the entire conversation. This drops cached tokens from hundreds of thousands (e.g. 440,000+ tokens) down to 0 or ~33,000 base tokens, causing massive latency spikes (TTFT 8s-15s vs 1.5s) and a 10x pricing penalty.

---

## Root Cause

In `internal/translator/gemini/openai/responses/gemini_openai-responses_request.go` (around line 95):

```go
case "message":
    if strings.EqualFold(itemRole, "system") || strings.EqualFold(itemRole, "developer") {
        pendingFunctionCallIDs = nil
        if contentArray := item.Get("content"); contentArray.Exists() {
            // ...
            part := []byte(`{"text":""}`)
            part, _ = sjson.SetBytes(part, "text", text)
            systemParts = append(systemParts, part)
        }
        continue
    }
```

Any `message` item with `role == "developer"` or `role == "system"` is unconditionally appended to `systemParts`, which becomes `request.systemInstruction`.

---

## Why and When Does Codex Emit Mid-Session Developer Messages? (Source: `openai/codex`)

Examining the newly open-sourced [`openai/codex`](https://github.com/openai/codex) codebase reveals that Codex's prompt construction is intentionally designed as an **Append-Only Diff stream** to maximize OpenAI's prefix prompt caching:

### Architectural Mechanism
1. In `codex-rs/core/src/context/world_state/mod.rs`, Codex models all environmental and policy states as `WorldStateSection`s. All fragments implement `ContextualUserFragment` where `role()` returns `"developer"`.
2. In `codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs:3411` (`merge_contextual_fragments`), before submitting a new turn, Codex computes `world_state.render_diff(&previous_snapshot)`.
3. Rather than modifying initial `instructions` or rewriting past history, Codex **appends only the diff** as a `ResponseItem::Message { role: "developer", ... }` directly to `input` preceding the user prompt.
4. In OpenAI's Responses API, prompt caching matches the longest matching token prefix. Because Codex appends diffs to the end of `input`, the entire historical prefix `input[0..N-1]` remains 100% bit-identical across turns.

### Key Scenarios Where Codex Injects Mid-Session `developer` Messages
In real-world usage, Codex emits mid-session `developer` messages across these common workflows:

1. **Image Resize Notices (`ImageResizeNotice`)** (`core/src/context/image_resize_notice.rs`):
   When a user pastes/attaches a large image or screenshot, Codex downscales it locally to save tokens and emits:
   ```xml
   <image_resize_notice>Image 1 of 1 was resized to 800x600</image_resize_notice>
   ```
   *(This is the most common trigger in multi-modal coding sessions).*
2. **Permission & Approval Policy Changes (`PermissionsState`)** (`core/src/context/world_state/permissions.rs`):
   When a user toggles approval policy (e.g., via `/approvals` or UI toggle from "Always ask" to "Never ask"), approves a persistent command prefix (`Approved command prefix saved: ["git", "diff"]`), or modifies sandbox writable roots:
   ```xml
   <permissions instructions>
   Approved command prefix saved: ["git", "diff"]
   </permissions instructions>
   ```
3. **Collaboration Mode Switching (`CollaborationModeInstructions`)** (`core/src/context/world_state/collaboration_mode.rs`):
   When switching between Default and Plan modes (e.g. `/plan`, `/default`):
   ```xml
   <collaboration_mode>
   # Collaboration Mode: Plan
   You are now in Plan mode...
   </collaboration_mode>
   ```
4. **Model & Reasoning Effort Switching (`ModelSwitchInstructions`)** (`core/src/context/world_state/model.rs`):
   When switching models or adjusting reasoning effort mid-thread (e.g., from medium to high):
   ```xml
   <model_switch>
   Active model changed to o3 with high reasoning effort.
   </model_switch>
   ```
5. **Multi-Agent & Subagent Notifications (`SubagentNotification`)** (`core/src/context/subagent_notification.rs`):
   When background subagents finish or fail, status updates are injected as developer messages:
   ```xml
   <subagent_notification>
   Subagent 019c... has completed its task with status: success.
   </subagent_notification>
   ```
6. **Token Budget & Context Window Warnings (`ContextWindowGuidance`)** (`core/src/context/token_budget_context.rs`):
   When approaching context limits or budget milestones:
   ```xml
   <context_window_guidance>
   Your context window is nearly exhausted (only 12,000 tokens remaining)...
   </context_window_guidance>
   ```
7. **Network Sandbox Proxy Rule Updates (`NetworkRuleSaved`)** (`core/src/context/network_rule_saved.rs`):
   When a domain access rule is granted/denied during tool execution.
8. **Guardian Security Audits (`GuardianReviewEvidenceFragment`)** (`core/src/context/guardian_review_evidence.rs`):
   Security audit evidence injected before/after sensitive shell/code execution.
9. **Auto-Compaction Summaries (`CompactionSummary`)** (`core/src/context/compaction_summary.rs`):
   When history is compacted, the structured checkpoint summary is appended as a developer message.

Because CPA currently hoists ALL of these into `systemInstruction`, **every single one of these common events wipes out 100% of the accumulated conversation cache on Gemini**.

---

## Upstream Google / Antigravity Wire Protocol Constraint

Direct probing against the upstream Antigravity endpoint (`daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com/v1internal:generateContent`) reveals that Google's wire parser strictly validates message roles in `contents`:

```text
HTTP 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT: Role 'developer' is not supported. Please use a valid role: MODEL, USER.
```

Google Gemini has no native `developer` role. In Google's own tools (`gemini-cli`, Cloud Code Assist) and in Anthropic's Claude Code (`<system_reminder>`), system-level mid-session instructions are always encapsulated in XML tags within `role: "user"` parts.

---

## Reproducible Evidence (Live Upstream Verification)

### Live Test with 41k-Token Codebase on `gemini-3.8-flash-high`

```text
Turn 1 (Cold Start):
  promptTokenCount: 41,028
  cachedContentTokenCount: 0

Turn 2 (Baseline follow-up, identical systemInstruction):
  promptTokenCount: 41,164
  cachedContentTokenCount: 36,821 (89.5% cache hit)

Turn 3A (CPA Current Behavior: Hoisting developer notice to systemInstruction):
  promptTokenCount: 41,210
  cachedContentTokenCount: 0 (Cache completely wiped out!)

Turn 3B (Proposed Fix: systemInstruction untouched, developer notice in contents as role: user):
  promptTokenCount: 41,209
  cachedContentTokenCount: 36,810 (89.3% cache hit preserved!)
```

### Sanitized Request Log Samples

#### Upstream Request (Step 2 - Normal Follow-up with Valid Cache)

```http
POST /v1internal:generateContent HTTP/1.1
```

#### Upstream Request (Step 3 - Hoisted Developer Message Destroys Cache)

```http

      "parts": [
        {"text": "You are an expert distributed systems engineer."},
        {"text": "<image_resize_notice>Image 1 of 1 was resized</image_resize_notice>"}
      ]
    },
    "contents": [
      {"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": "<50k tokens base codebase>"}]},
      {"role": "model", "parts": [{"text": "SYSTEM_READY"}]},
      {"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": "What is the buffer size?"}]},
      {"role": "model", "parts": [{"text": "5000"}]},
      {"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": "What is the struct name?"}]}
    ]
  },
  "model": "gemini-3.8-flash-high"
}
```

**Upstream Response (Usage Metadata):**
```json
{
  "usageMetadata": {
    "promptTokenCount": 55137,
    "candidatesTokenCount": 53,
    "totalTokenCount": 55190
  }
}
```
*(Notice `cachedContentTokenCount` is completely absent / 0, because `systemInstruction` changed.)*

---

## Production Impact

In long-running Codex sessions with 400k+ tokens:
- At Turn N (e.g. `usage_event` ID `108122`), cache hit is **437,667 / 442,042 tokens (99.0%)**.
- At Turn N+1 (ID `108123`), the user pastes a screenshot, causing Codex to inject `<image_resize_notice>` as a developer message.
- Cache instantly drops from 437k tokens to **33,011 tokens (7.4%)**, forcing **412,178 tokens** of unnecessary full-price re-prefill.

---

## Proposed Fix

In `ConvertOpenAIResponsesRequestToGemini` (and similarly in Chat Completions `gemini_openai_request.go`):
1. Maintain a state flag `hasEncounteredConversation := false`.
2. Only hoist `developer` or `system` messages that appear **before the first `user` / `assistant` / `model` message** into `systemInstruction` (the true initial system prompt).
3. Once conversation has begun (`hasEncounteredConversation == true`), any subsequent `developer` or `system` message must **NOT** mutate `systemInstruction`.
4. Instead, retain it in `contents` with `role: "user"` at its original sequential position (optionally coalescing adjacent user parts).
5. This guarantees that `systemInstruction` remains strictly immutable across the entire session, ensuring Gemini prompt cache hit rates of 90%~99% throughout multi-turn Codex workflows.

v8 management: plugin quota contract gaps (quota plugin lookup & quota_probe)

## 背景

管理面板 issue router-for-me/Cli-Proxy-API-Management-Center#491：面板的通用插件额度卡调用 `POST /v8/management/quota/fetch`，但 v8 下没有这个路由，所以返回 404。面板这边已经改为先通过 `GET /v8/management/plugins` 找到插件 id，再调用 `POST /v8/management/plugins/:id/quota`。迁移过程中发现 v8 的契约还有两处缺口，前端单独补不上。

以下引用基于 `dev`（与 v8.0.23 相同，下面涉及的文件都没有改动）。

## 1. `GET /v8/management/plugins` 没有暴露插件支持的 provider 列表

凭证列表只返回 `supports_quota` 和 `quota_provider: <auth.Provider>`（`internal/api/handlers/management/auth_files.go:680-693`），不包含插件 id，而 v8 只能按插件 id 查询额度（`/plugins/:id/quota`）。

后端 `quotaProviderRecord`（`internal/pluginhost/quota_provider.go:157`）分两轮匹配：

1. 第一轮按 `QuotaProvider.Identifier()`、插件 id、`AuthProvider.Identifier()` 匹配。这三个字段 `/plugins` 都有返回（`quota_provider`、`id`、`oauth_provider`），前端可以照着实现。
2. 第二轮按 `DescribeQuota` 返回的 `SupportedProviders` 匹配。这个列表 `/plugins` 没有返回（`pluginListEntry` 与 `RegisteredPluginInfo` 都没有对应字段）。

因此，如果插件只通过 `SupportedProviders` 声明支持某个 provider，并且装了不止一个额度插件，前端就无法确定该调用哪个插件。

**建议（任选一种）：**
- 在 `/plugins` 每一项中加入 `quota_supported_providers`（复用 `cachedQuotaSupportedProviders` 的结果）；或者
- 在凭证列表的条目中直接返回匹配到的 `quota_plugin_id`。在 `ListAuthFiles` 计算 `supports_quota` 时就已经可以拿到 record，第二种方式对前端最简单，也和后端的匹配顺序完全一致。

## 2. 声明式 `quota_probe` 在 v8 下没有对应接口

- 只要凭证 metadata 中带有 `quota_probe`，凭证列表就会返回 `supports_quota: true`（`auth_files.go:695-699`）。
- 执行 probe 的逻辑只在 v0 的 `FetchCredentialQuota` 里作为兜底（`internal/api/handlers/management/plugin_quota.go:114-128`），对应 `POST /v0/management/quota/fetch`。
- v8 只注册了 `/plugins/:id/quota`（`internal/api/server_management_v8.go:60-62`），而它的处理函数 `fetchQuotaForPlugin` 要求插件存在，不会执行 probe。`server_management_v8_test.go:116-124` 也明确断言 `credentials/quota/{providers,fetch,reset}` 在 v8 下返回 404。

结果是：v8 宣告了这类凭证支持额度，却没有接口可以查询。面板目前只能显示"v8 管理接口暂不支持声明式额度探测"。

**建议：** 二选一：
- 为 v8 提供一个执行 `quota_probe` 的接口，例如 `POST /v8/management/credentials/quota/probe`，请求体为 `{auth_index}`；
- 如果 v8 不再支持 `quota_probe`，就不要因为 `quota_probe` 而返回 `supports_quota`。

## 参考

- 面板端提交：router-for-me/Cli-Proxy-API-Management-Center@ec9fc974（内置额度卡优先于插件额度）、router-for-me/Cli-Proxy-API-Management-Center@390718ec（改用 `/plugins/:id/quota`）。

aistudio executor: one SSE frame split across multiple relay chunks (large `thoughtSignature`) → no `finish_reason`, "upstream stream closed before any chunk carried finish_reason"

## Version

CLIProxyAPI v8.0.47 (commit 90c447d), provider `aistudio` (WebSocket relay). This already includes #6978 (`3078035`, "translate every SSE frame of a relay chunk").

## Summary

With `gemini-3.6-flash` streaming through the `aistudio` provider, `/v1/chat/completions` always ends with an error frame and no `finish_reason`, although the upstream request succeeded (usage recorded, HTTP 200, `finishReason: "STOP"` is present upstream).

`gemini-3.5-flash-lite` on the same channel is fine, because it does not emit a large `thoughtSignature`.

## Reproduce

```bash
curl -N https://<host>/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gemini-3.6-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi in 5 words"}],"max_tokens":60,"stream":true}'
```

Reproduced 3/3. Output:

```
data: {... "delta":{"content":"Hi there! How are you?"}, "finish_reason":null ...}
data: {... "delta":{"content":""}, "finish_reason":null ...}
data: {"error":{"message":"upstream stream closed before any chunk carried finish_reason","type":"server_error","code":"internal_server_error"}}
```

The client sees a truncated stream with no `finish_reason` and no `[DONE]`.

## Evidence (raw upstream captured with `request-log: true`)

The final SSE event carries `"finishReason":"STOP"` plus a ~3.7 KB `thoughtSignature`. In the API RESPONSE section it arrives as 4 separate chunks (split on blank lines):

| # | len | content |
|---|----:|---|
| 2 | 1181 | `data: {"candidates":[{"content":{"parts":[{"text":"","thoughtSignature":"EuESCt4S...` (cut mid-signature) |
| 3 | 1186 | `ttiQ8mm2NDgj...` (no `data:` prefix, mid-signature) |
| 4 | 1186 | `4f1yghMfPRY3...` ... `": 653,"serviceTier": "standard"},"model` |
| 5 | 69 | `Version": "gemini-3.6-flash","responseId": "..."}` |

Segments before it (#0, #1, ~380 bytes each) are complete `data: {...}` events and valid JSON. Segment #2 alone is invalid JSON; segments #3–#5 are orphan fragments that do not start with `data:`. Concatenating #2–#5 yields valid JSON with `candidates[0].finishReason == "STOP"`.

So the split point is a fixed ~1.18 KB boundary inside one SSE frame, i.e. one frame is split across several relay chunks.

## Cause (as far as I can tell)

The aistudio executor treats each relay chunk as a complete SSE frame (or as a set of complete frames, per #6978). When one frame spans several chunks:

- the first fragment is parsed leniently and yields an empty delta (the `content: ""` chunk seen by the client),
- the remaining fragments have no `data:` prefix and are dropped,
- `sawFinishReason` never becomes true, so the truncation guard fires (`upstream stream closed before any chunk carried finish_reason`).

#6978 handles "one chunk containing several frames"; this is the inverse case, "one frame spread over several chunks".

I cannot tell from the cliproxy side whether the splitting happens in the Applet/relay or in the WS transport; cliproxy just receives the chunks.

## Suggested fix

In `internal/runtime/executor/aistudio_executor.go` `ExecuteStream`, buffer relay chunk payloads and only translate once a full SSE frame is available (i.e. up to a blank line `\n\n`), carrying the remainder over to the next chunk, and flush the remainder on stream end. Alternatively, if the chunk is not a complete `data:` frame, append it to the pending buffer instead of translating it.

## Side notes

- `/v1/messages` (Claude format) on the same model looks fine, probably because the stream end synthesizes `end_turn`; I did not verify that the signature is intact there.
- Related but different: #6906 (non-content terminations reported as truncation).

[Bug]: High idle CPU usage caused by busy-polling in credential concurrency release flush loop (v8.0.48)

**Is it a request payload issue?**
[ ] Yes, this is a request payload issue. I am using a client/cURL to send a request payload, but I received an unexpected error.
[x] No, it's another issue.

**Describe the bug**
In v8.0.48, when running with a moderate/large account pool (~150 credential `.json` files in `auth-dir`), `CLIProxyAPI` consumes continuous high CPU (100%–140%+ on a 2-core Linux VM) **even when totally idle with 0 active in-flight requests**.

Inspecting the process threads via `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/stack` indicates that multiple background Go goroutines are constantly spinning across all credentials acquiring/releasing futex locks:
```text
[<0>] futex_do_wait+0x37/0x70
[<0>] __futex_wait+0x90/0x100
[<0>] futex_wait+0x66/0x100
[<0>] do_futex+0x138/0x1d0
[<0>] __x64_sys_futex+0x73/0x1d0
```
This is triggered by the credential concurrency ticker (`release-flush-interval: 250ms` and `busy-retry-min: 250ms`). The ticker unconditionally traverses and synchronizes locks across every credential entry in the pool on every tick, regardless of whether there are any actual in-flight requests or pending releases.

codex, claude code (multi-account pool with ~150 credential files)

**Model Name**
All models (occurs in the Credential Concurrency & In-Flight Management layer)

**LLM Client**
Idle state / Any client (VS Code, Codex Desktop, etc.)

**Request Information**
The high CPU issue occurs even with **0 client requests** (completely idle).

```bash
# Yet container CPU remains pinned at 100%+:
docker stats cli-proxy-api --no-stream
```

**Expected behavior**
1. When there are no active in-flight requests (`in_flight == 0`) and no credentials to release, background tickers for `release-flush-interval` and `snapshot-interval` should sleep or skip lock iteration.
2. Idle CPU consumption should be near 0.0% when no client requests are being served.

**Screenshots**
N/A

**OS Type**

 - Version: Kernel 5.14+, Docker 27.x

**Additional context**

  Relaxing the intervals in `config.yaml` drops idle CPU from 140% to ~0.0%:
  ```yaml

    concurrency:
      release-flush-interval: 1s    # relaxed from 250ms
      busy-retry-min: 500ms         # relaxed from 250ms
      busy-retry-max: 2s            # relaxed from 1s
    in-flight:
      snapshot-interval: 10s        # relaxed from 2s
      stale-after: 35s
  ```
- **Suggested code fix**:
  In the background goroutine handling `release-flush-interval`, consider checking whether in-flight count is 0 before acquiring locks:
  ```go
  if atomic.LoadInt64(&globalInFlight) == 0 && releaseQueue.Len() == 0 {
  ```
