[Proposal]: Normalize brand-source provenance links for shared diagrams

## Goal

Give shared diagrams a clean, useful brand-source link without copying request-specific URL data into the visible provenance or generated markup.

## Proposed scope

Separate the URL needed to fetch and verify a remote brand asset from the public source URL recorded in the diagram. Keep digest-pinned fetching unchanged; use a normalized HTTP(S) source link suitable for sharing.

For the public provenance, omit userinfo, query strings and fragments. This proposal is about display/share metadata, not changing the actual fetch URL or silently invalidating existing pins.

## Acceptance and compatibility

- Use synthetic URL values only in tests.
- Verify node metadata and SVG/HTML provenance consistently use the normalized public link.
- Preserve the fetch URL, captured asset bytes, digest validation, redirects policy and built-in brand behavior.
- Keep enough origin/path information for the source link to remain useful; document any cases where a canonical landing-page link would be more appropriate.

Prefer a small shared normalization helper over changes to the fetching pipeline.

[Bug]: Checker ENOBUFS with status 0 can be reported as CLI success

## Problem

On pinned dev `e23fc2c5c8cf1aaa3864e7966f8b8ec43dc2bebd`, checker output overflow can be reported as CLI success. Node's `spawnSync` sometimes returns `error.code = ENOBUFS` together with `status = 0`. The CLI checks `status !== 0` before classifying the error, so that combination bypasses the existing `artifact/check-output-limit` diagnostic.

This was found during #742/#743 validation; their Workflow changes do not modify the CLI, checker, Architecture input or affected tests.

## Reproduction

Git checkout, macOS arm64, official Node 22.23.2. The input is the checked-in public `archify/examples/web-app.architecture.json`; no private JSON is needed.

```sh
ARCHIFY_CHECK_MAX_BUFFER=1024 node archify/bin/archify.mjs validate architecture archify/examples/web-app.architecture.json --json
```

Repeat the command: the condition is intermittent. Paired read-only probes observed false success in 2/10 calls on pinned dev and 3/10 calls on #743 head `808de451`; these counts establish reproduction, not a frequency estimate.

Observed inner checker result in a false-success call:

```json
{"error":"ENOBUFS","status":0,"signal":null,"stdoutBytes":3406,"configuredLimitBytes":1024}
```

The outer CLI exited 0 with `ok: true`. Other calls correctly exited 1 with `artifact/check-output-limit`. The same output-limit family also caused the existing deliver-order regression to fail during #742's full suite; that exact deliver failure was not separately reproduced on the base.

## Expected behavior

A checker transport/spawn error takes precedence over its exit status. Overflow must exit nonzero and emit `artifact/check-output-limit`, including `ENOBUFS`, received bytes and configured limit. Delivery must preserve the previous artifact and record failure before retiring staging.

## Scope and acceptance

- Check `result.error` before interpreting successful exit status in all checker callers; keep successful complete receipts unchanged.
- Add deterministic coverage for `ENOBUFS + status: 0`, so testing does not depend on winning a process scheduling race.
- Retain public CLI validate and deliver preservation regressions; audit migrate/compare callers without assuming they have already been reproduced.

Existing conditions: [validate](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/blob/e23fc2c5c8cf1aaa3864e7966f8b8ec43dc2bebd/archify/bin/archify.mjs#L6937), [deliver](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/blob/e23fc2c5c8cf1aaa3864e7966f8b8ec43dc2bebd/archify/bin/archify.mjs#L4841). This is related to #525/#590 but distinct: those report valid diagrams falsely failing because of the buffer limit; this issue reports an existing overflow error incorrectly treated as success.

[Bug]: Architecture component-level failures report empty subject/evidence/supportedFixes while their messages carry the repair

## Problem

`architecture` renderer diagnostics for component-level failures arrive with every structured field empty, even though each message already carries the measured repair. With `validate --json`:

- `subject` is only `{"diagramType":"architecture"}` — it does not name the affected component (or pair),
- `evidence` is `{}` — none of the numbers the message itself already computed,
- `supportedFixes` is `[]` — although the message ends in a concrete repair, e.g. `Suggested fix: move "right" pos to [248, 40] (right of "left") or [244, 128] (below)`.

`references/authoring-contract.md` tells agents to "Consume `diagnostics[]` by stable `code`, exact `subject`, measured `evidence`, and `supportedFixes`". For these four failure kinds the documented repair loop has nothing to act on and the free-text message is the only signal, while the sibling families already carry the fields — `layout/boundary-out-of-bounds`, `layout/route-out-of-bounds`, `composition/label-gap` in the same renderer, and `sequence/participant-label-overflow` in the sequence renderer.

Affected kinds (all fall back to the untyped `layout/constraint` default):

1. Component falls outside the viewBox.
2. Two components closer than 8px (the message already includes a two-coordinate suggestion).
3. Label wider than its component.
4. Sublabel/tag unreadable at the legible minimum.

## Reproduction

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "diagram_type": "architecture",
  "meta": { "title": "Component diagnostics probe", "output": "probe.html", "quality_profile": "standard", "viewBox": [640, 360] },
  "components": [
    { "id": "left",    "type": "backend",  "label": "Left", "pos": [40, 40],   "size": [200, 80] },
    { "id": "right",   "type": "backend",  "label": "Right", "pos": [244, 40],  "size": [200, 80] },
    { "id": "outside", "type": "database", "label": "Outside", "pos": [520, 300], "size": [200, 80] },
    { "id": "narrow",  "type": "backend",  "label": "A Deliberately Long Label", "pos": [40, 180], "size": [56, 80], "sublabel": "A very long sublabel that cannot possibly fit" }
  ],
  "connections": []
}
```

`node archify/bin/archify.mjs validate architecture <file> --json` → 4 diagnostics, each
`code: "layout/constraint"`, `subject: {"diagramType":"architecture"}`, `evidence: {}`, `supportedFixes: []`.

## Actual (verbatim messages; the fields shown above are empty on all four)

1. `Component "outside" falls outside the viewBox 640x360 — adjust pos/size or set a larger meta.viewBox.`
2. `Label "A Deliberately Long Label" (~165px) is wider than component "narrow" (56px) — shorten the label or widen size.`
3. `Sublabel "A very long sublabel that cannot possibly fit" needs ~162px at the 6px legible minimum, but component "narrow" provides 48px — shorten the sublabel or widen size.`
4. Multi-line: `Components "left" and "right" are less than 8px apart — move one or shrink its size.` plus the two-line bounds/suggestion hint.

The same empty fields appear in `render`/`deliver` failure receipts, under `layout.mode: "grid"`, and under `quality_profile: "showcase"`.

## Expected

The four kinds carry the affected component (or pair) in `subject`, the numbers the message already computes in `evidence`, and the concrete repair(s) in `supportedFixes`, following the same contract as the sibling diagnostics listed above.

Environment: `dev` 9ef0961, Node 22.23.1, repo checkout.

[Bug]: Preview refresh loses the last verified diagram while a source edit needs fixing

### Version and environment

Reproduced on `dev` at `96234021b5d743d1b730875b9b46de9fba2a7633`, macOS, Node 22.23.1 and real Chrome.

### Problem

Preview keeps the last verified artifact when a source edit fails. However, refreshing the preview page or opening another tab during that failure loses the visible diagram. The header claims `Needs fix · showing rev 1`, while the canvas says it is waiting for its first verified diagram.

The server still reports revision 1 with `lastVerified` in `/state`, and `/artifact.html` returns the complete verified HTML (HTTP 200). Only client initialization is wrong: the iframe has no `src`, remains hidden and the body has `data-has-artifact="false"`.

### Reproduction

Use a temporary directory; do not corrupt the checked-in example:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/archify-preview-repro
cp archify/examples/web-app.architecture.json /tmp/archify-preview-repro/source.json
node archify/bin/archify.mjs preview architecture /tmp/archify-preview-repro/source.json /tmp/archify-preview-repro/diagram.html --no-open
```

1. Open the printed loopback URL and wait for `Verified · rev 1`.
2. In another terminal, replace the temporary source with incomplete JSON:

   ```sh
   printf '{"meta":' > /tmp/archify-preview-repro/source.json
   ```

3. Wait for `Needs fix`. The existing tab correctly keeps the diagram.
4. Refresh the page or open the same preview URL in a new tab. It now has a blank placeholder despite the header claiming the old revision is being shown.
5. Stop the preview with Ctrl-C when finished.

### Expected and bounded approach

Every connected preview client should display the last verified artifact, including a new client arriving in `needs-fix` or `checking`. A session that has never verified anything should retain the empty placeholder. Identical revision updates should not reload the iframe and discard Viewer state; a newly verified revision should still load normally.

Separate artifact restoration from the current build-status presentation in the preview shell. Preserve failure diagnostics, server protocol, last-good publication rules, loopback behavior and standalone generated artifacts. Cover state transitions plus a real-browser late-client reproduction.

REST API auth errors are sent as `text/plain`, so JSON clients can't read them

### Check before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and did not find a duplicate

### Describe the bug

When the REST gateway (`/api/v1/*`) refuses a request in its auth middleware, the body is JSON but the response says `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Clients that check the content type before parsing can't read the error.

We hit this with [MoeMemos](https://github.com/mudkipme/MoeMemos) on iOS. While its access token wasn't being accepted, all it showed was "unexpected content type, expected JSON", so the real message ("authentication required") never reached us. It looked like a server crash rather than an auth problem.

Other gateway errors are `application/json`. I checked a 404 and a 501 from the same gateway, and the throttle refusal right after the auth check goes through `writeGatewayStatusError`, which sets the JSON header.

**What happened:** `401` with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8` and a JSON body.
**What I expected:** `401` with `Content-Type: application/json` and the same body shape as other gateway errors (`{"code":16,"message":"authentication required","details":[]}`).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run Memos with default settings: `docker run -d -p 127.0.0.1:5230:5230 neosmemo/memos:0.31.0`
2. Call a protected REST endpoint without a token (or with an invalid one):
   ```
   curl -i http://127.0.0.1:5230/api/v1/auth/me
   curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer memos_pat_invalid' http://127.0.0.1:5230/api/v1/auth/me
   ```
3. See:
   ```
   HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
   Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate
   Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
   X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
   Content-Length: 51

   {"code": 16, "message": "authentication required"}
   ```
4. Compare with a 404 from the same gateway (`curl -i http://127.0.0.1:5230/api/v1/does-not-exist`), which is `Content-Type: application/json` with `{"code":5, "message":"Not Found", "details":[]}`.

### Memos version

v0.31.0 (Docker `neosmemo/memos:0.31.0`). The same code is on main@0bfa31e.

### Additional context

**Deployment:** Docker Desktop on macOS, SQLite, behind `tailscale serve`. Client: MoeMemos on iOS.

#### Cause

`writeGatewayAuthorizationError` writes its responses with `http.Error`, which always sets `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and appends a newline to the body. The body is a hand-written JSON string, so it also differs slightly from the gateway's other errors (no `details`).

- main: [`server/api/api.go#L336-L343`](https://github.com/usememos/memos/blob/0bfa31e89ec550c7cc6a1dea3888af2d0de107c2/server/api/api.go#L336-L343), called from the gateway auth middleware at [L170](https://github.com/usememos/memos/blob/0bfa31e89ec550c7cc6a1dea3888af2d0de107c2/server/api/api.go#L170)
- v0.31.0: [`server/api/v1/v1.go#L306-L313`](https://github.com/usememos/memos/blob/v0.31.0/server/api/v1/v1.go#L306-L313)

Both branches of that function are affected: the 401 and the 500 ("failed to resolve API access policy"). The fallback in `writeGatewayStatusError`, used when the status can't be marshalled ([main L328](https://github.com/usememos/memos/blob/0bfa31e89ec550c7cc6a1dea3888af2d0de107c2/server/api/api.go#L328)), uses `http.Error` the same way.

#### Candidate fix

Route the auth errors through `writeGatewayStatusError`, which the throttle refusal three lines later already uses. That way they get the same header and body shape as every other gateway error:

```go
func writeGatewayAuthorizationError(w http.ResponseWriter, err error) {
	if errors.Is(err, ErrUnauthenticated) {
		writeGatewayStatusError(w, status.Error(codes.Unauthenticated, "authentication required"))
		return
	}
	slog.Error("failed to resolve API access policy", "error", err)
	writeGatewayStatusError(w, status.Error(codes.Internal, "failed to resolve API access policy"))
}
```

And in `writeGatewayStatusError`, write the marshal-failure fallback directly rather than through `http.Error`:

```go
if marshalErr != nil {
	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusInternalServerError)
	_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"code":13,"message":"failed to encode error","details":[]}`))
	return
}
```

A gateway 401 case in `server/testdata/http_compat.jsonl` would pin this. The file already has one for `/api/sse`, which correctly returns `application/json`. I haven't built or tested this patch. The repro above was run against v0.31.0, and I read the code on main.

ImageResponse fails after an uncached next/image optimization

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/ceolinwill/next-image-response-repro

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the reproduction and start a production server:

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm start
```

2. In another terminal, request the `ImageResponse` route:

```sh
curl -o /dev/null -w 'OG before: %{http_code}\n' http://localhost:3000/og
```

This returns `200`.

3. Perform one uncached image optimization:

```sh
image_id="$(node -p 'crypto.randomUUID()')"
curl -D - -o /dev/null "http://localhost:3000/_next/image?url=%2Fpixel%2F${image_id}&w=640&q=75"
```

This returns `200` with `X-Nextjs-Cache: MISS`

4. Request the same `ImageResponse` route again:

```sh
curl -v -o /dev/null http://localhost:3000/og
```

The server closes the connection without returning a response.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

On Next.js 16.3.0, the `/og` route initially returns a valid PNG with status `200`.

After the same server process handles one cache-miss request through the Next.js image optimizer, subsequent calls to `/og` fail with an empty response. The server logs:

```text
Error: failed to pipe response
[cause]: Error: Input buffer contains unsupported image format
```

I expected `ImageResponse` to continue returning the same valid PNG regardless of whether the server previously handled an image optimization request.

### Provide environment information

```bash

  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.6.0: Sat Jul 11 15:27:27 PDT 2026; root:xnu-12377.161.13~4/RELEASE_ARM64_T6041
  Available memory (MB): 65536
  Available CPU cores: 16
Binaries:
  Node: 24.12.0
  npm: 11.6.2
  Yarn: N/A

Relevant Packages:

  eslint-config-next: N/A

  react-dom: 19.2.8
  typescript: N/A
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Image (next/image), Metadata, Runtime

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next start (local)

### Additional context

The failure is order-dependent and appears to affect the entire server process:

- Opening `/og` directly works before the image optimizer is invoked.
- Only an optimizer cache miss triggers the failure. A cached request with `X-Nextjs-Cache: HIT` does not reproduce it.
- Restarting the server resets the behavior until another uncached optimization occurs.
- The reproduction does not import `sharp` directly and has no custom Next.js configuration.

I also tested `next@canary` on August 4, 2026 and the issue does not reproduce there: both `/og` requests return `200`. The regression is present in stable `16.3.0`.

### Possible regression source

This appears related to #96301.

That PR added a process-wide Sharp loader policy that first blocks `VipsForeignLoad` and then unblocks the HEIF, JPEG, GIF, PNG, TIFF, and WebP loaders. It does not unblock `VipsForeignLoadSvg`.

Node.js `ImageResponse` generates SVG internally and then passes that SVG to the same Sharp module to produce the PNG. After an uncached `next/image` request initializes Sharp with the new raster-only allowlist, `ImageResponse` can no longer load its generated SVG.

This change is present in Next.js 16.3.0 but absent from 16.3.0-preview.10, where the reproduction continues returning `200`.

I also reproduced the mechanism directly with the bundled Sharp version:

- SVG rendering works before applying the loader policy.
- Applying the allowlist from #96301 causes `Input buffer contains unsupported image format`.
- Unblocking `VipsForeignLoadSvg` restores SVG rendering.

Root cause

.next/types/cache-life.d.ts has no top-level import or export, so it is a script, not a module.
That makes its `declare module 'next/cache' { ... }` a standalone ambient module declaration
rather than a module augmentation — it shadows node_modules/next/cache.d.ts instead of merging
with it, which is why it has to re-export every other next/cache member.

  after build:   "next/cache" -> .next/types/cache-life.d.ts   (package types shadowed)

exporting those names. Both modules are therefore offered under the specifier next/cache,
producing two identical entries per export.

The file is written by next build, next dev and next typegen, so this is not build-specific:

- next/dist/build/index.js  (distDir/types/cache-life.d.ts)

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

### To Reproduce

```bash

curl http://localhost:3900/api/probe                # hangs forever
```

The route (`app/api/probe/route.js`) does nothing but open a raw
`net.Socket` (no `fetch`, no HTTP) to a plain TCP echo server, write a byte,
and await the echo:

```js
import net from "node:net";

function probeRawSocket(port) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const socket = net.createConnection({ host: "127.0.0.1", port }, () => {
      socket.write("ping");
    });
    socket.on("data", (data) => {
      socket.end();
      resolve(data.toString());
    });
    socket.on("error", reject);
  });
}

export async function GET() {
  const start = Date.now();
  const reply = await probeRawSocket(Number(process.env.ECHO_PORT));
  return Response.json({ reply, ms: Date.now() - start });
}
```

`next.config.js` only sets:

```js
module.exports = {
  experimental: {
    testProxy: process.env.ENABLE_TEST_PROXY === "true",
  },
};
```

### Current vs. Expected behavior

With `experimental.testProxy: true` on **Next.js 16.3.0**, the request to
`/api/probe` never resolves — no response, no error, no timeout. Confirmed
via `lsof` on the `next-server` process that the outbound TCP connection to
the echo server is never even opened at the socket level.

With the exact same code and env, only changing the version:

| next version | testProxy | result |
|---|---|---|
| 16.2.12 | true | resolves in ~6ms |
| 16.3.0 | true | **hangs forever** |
| 16.3.0 | false | resolves in ~3ms |

Expected: `testProxy` should only intercept `fetch()`/HTTP traffic (per its
documented purpose for `next/experimental/testmode`), and should not affect
unrelated raw `net.Socket` connections — matching the 16.2.12 behavior.

### Real-world impact

We hit this via `next/experimental/testmode/playwright/msw`, which flips this
same flag on to let Playwright/MSW intercept `fetch()` calls in e2e tests.
One of our API routes also runs a normal `pg` (`node-postgres`) query in the
same request. After upgrading 16.2.12 → 16.3.0, every Playwright test whose
setup hits that route now hangs until Playwright's default 30s hook timeout,
and with retries + a single CI worker this silently burns ~90 minutes before
the job reports failure — with no actual error surfaced anywhere. We
confirmed with `pg_stat_activity`/`lsof` that Postgres never receives a
connection attempt while stuck.

This minimal repro shows it's not `pg`-specific — any raw socket traffic
appears to be swallowed by `testProxy` in 16.3.0 rather than passed through.

Turbopack panics in ModuleGraphImportTracer: 'entered unreachable code: there must be a path to a root' (module_graph/mod.rs:750)

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/agentHits/next-prerender-workstore-reproduction

### To Reproduce

1. Clone reproduction repository:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/agentHits/next-prerender-workstore-reproduction.git
cd next-prerender-workstore-reproduction
bun install # or npm install
```
2. Run a cold static export build without `experimental.inlineCss: true`:
```bash
rm -rf .next
bun run build # or next build
```
3. On projects with standalone output and complex CSS/SCSS modules, Turbopack panics in the Rust runtime:
```text
thread 'tokio-rt-worker' panicked at turbopack/crates/turbopack-core/src/module_graph/mod.rs:750:25:
internal error: entered unreachable code: there must be a path to a root

Debug info:
- Execution of emit_all_output_assets_once_with_issues_operation failed
- Execution of PlainIssue::from_issue failed
- Execution of <ModuleGraphImportTracer as ImportTracer>::get_traces failed
- internal error: entered unreachable code: there must be a path to a root
```

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current Behavior:**
When formatting an issue/warning trace during CSS chunk emission (`emit_all_output_assets_once_with_issues`), `ModuleGraphImportTracer::get_traces` executes `astar` searching for a node with no incoming edges in the reversed graph (`|n| reversed_graph.neighbors(n).next().is_none()`).
If the module subgraph contains cyclic references or disconnected nodes, `astar` returns `None`, triggering the panic `unreachable!("there must be a path to a root")` at line 750, terminating the entire build process.

To avoid this crash, developers are forced to enable `experimental.inlineCss: true`, which bypasses external CSS chunking by serializing all CSS text chunks directly into the RSC Flight stream (`self.__next_f`), inflating document HTML size from ~150 KB to >700 KB and causing significant Core Web Vitals regressions (LCP: 8.9s vs 2.1s).

**Expected Behavior:**
Turbopack should handle cyclic or rootless subgraphs gracefully by falling back to returning the current module index instead of panicking.

let path = match petgraph::algo::astar(
    &reversed_graph,
    module_idx,
    |n| reversed_graph.neighbors(n).next().is_none(),

cachedNavigations session-shell prerender races an async cacheHandlers.default get: E1163 on every dynamic render with deterministic keys

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/vicanera/next-cached-navigations-cache-handler-race

### To Reproduce

1. Next 16.3.4, `cacheComponents: true`, `partialPrefetching: true`, and a `cacheHandlers.default` whose `get` awaits I/O. In the linked repo `slow-cache-handler.js` wraps Next's own default in-memory handler and adds a few milliseconds of latency to `get` at runtime, standing in for a Redis/Memcached handler.
2. A page whose cached reads arrive in more than one batch (a second batch of `"use cache"` reads starts only after the first batch has resolved), with a cookie-bound child behind `<Suspense>` so the route is a dynamic render with a static shell.
3. `next build && next start`, then request the page repeatedly with `NEXT_PRIVATE_DEBUG_CACHE=1`.

In a production app with this configuration and a Redis-backed handler, roughly half of the renders of the affected page log three `E1163` warnings (one per cached read in the second batch); routes whose reads all start in one batch never do. Fallback-param renders additionally log `NEXT_STATIC_GEN_BAILOUT` ("Next.js encountered uncached or runtime data during prerendering") from the same spawned prerender.

Honest status of the linked repo: the isolated shape there has not yet fired the warning locally (0/30 at 5 ms and 20 ms handler latency). The debug trail below is from the production app on the same Next version; the exact batching that opens the window has not been reduced further. Included because the source-level mechanism is deterministic and the workaround is verified.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current.** With `experimental.cachedNavigations` (auto-enabled under `cacheComponents`) and Partial Prefetching on, every dynamic render (`renderToStream` for documents, `generateStagedDynamicFlightRenderResultNode` for RSC navigations) installs a `CacheSignal` and, on `cacheSignal.cacheReady()`, spawns `spawnRuntimePrefetchWithFilledCaches` (mode `rewindable-session-shell`). `cacheReady()` is a quiescence heuristic (`cache-signal.js`: read count 0 → `setImmediate` → `setTimeout(0)` with no new `beginRead`). In `use-cache-wrapper.js`, a cache-handler **hit** is written into the resume data cache only after `await cacheHandler.get()` (the "leader resolved with cache handler hit" path), whereas a generated entry is registered before the function runs (`saveToResumeDataCache`). So when a render's reads come in two batches, the count touches zero between them; with an async handler the spawned prerender then looks keys up while the second batch's `get`s are still pending, misses, warns:

```
Error: Unexpected cache miss after cache warming phase during prerendering. This is likely caused by non-deterministic arguments ...   (E1163)
```

and demotes the segment to a runtime hole. Every miss shows the same ordering for the affected key (`NEXT_PRIVATE_DEBUG_CACHE=1`):

```
use-cache: Resume Data Cache entry not found [key]        <- the render's own lookup
use-cache: registering as intra-request invocation leader [key]
use-cache: registering as cross-request invocation leader [key]
use-cache: Resume Data Cache entry not found [key]        <- the spawned prerender's lookup
Error: Unexpected cache miss after cache warming phase during prerendering ...
use-cache: leader resolved with cache handler hit [key]   <- the handler get resolves last
```

A request that does not miss shows `leader resolved with cache handler hit` before the second lookup. The arguments are deterministic; the message's diagnosis (non-deterministic arguments) does not apply. With the default in-memory handler `get` resolves within the same tick, so the race never shows there.

**Expected.** No warning and no demotion when cache keys are deterministic and the handler simply takes a few milliseconds. Either the pending handler read should hold the `CacheSignal` until the entry is registered in the resume data cache, or a handler hit should be registered in the resume data cache as a pending entry before the `get` is awaited, as the generated-entry path already does.

**Workaround.** `experimental: { cachedNavigations: false }` → 0 warnings over 85 requests in the production app; prefetch-driven navigations (`next-router-prefetch` 2/3, which take `generateRuntimePrefetchResult`) unaffected. The same code shape is present in `16.4.0-canary.26`.

PET always probes /usr/bin/python3, forcing CLT install on macOS

### Reproduction steps

1. On macOS WITHOUT Xcode Command Line Tools installed (/usr/bin/python3 is Apple's CLT stub, `xcode-select -p` fails)
2. Manage Python via Nix with PATH set to put it first (launchctl getenv PATH → /Users/development/.nix-profile/bin first)
3. Open a Python project in Zed (or trigger toolchain discovery)
4. Observe repeated log lines and the macOS "install command line developer tools" dialog

### Current vs. Expected behavior

```
Current behavior:
  Zed's Python toolchain discovery (via the `pet` library, Microsoft's
  python-environment-tools) unconditionally probes /usr/bin/python3 by
  absolute path. On a machine without Xcode Command Line Tools, that file
  is Apple's CLT stub: it prints the xcode-select install notice, exits 1,
  and emits no stdout. Zed logs:

    ERROR [pet_python_utils::env] Python Execution for "/usr/bin/python3" produced an output "" without a separator
    WARN  [pet::find] Unknown Python Env "/usr/bin/python3"

  and macOS repeatedly shows the "install command line developer tools"
  dialog. The probe is PATH-independent, so a managed Python (Nix/uv/
  pyenv) that is first in PATH does not prevent it.

  This effectively forces every macOS user who opens a Python project in
  Zed to install Apple's Command Line Tools — and therefore to accept the
  Apple license agreement — even when they manage Python entirely via
  Nix/uv/pyenv and want nothing to do with Apple's toolchain.

Expected behavior:
  The `MacCommandLineTools` locator (and `/usr/bin/python3` probing) should
  be disabled/skipped, so /usr/bin/python3 is never executed and no CLT
  install is ever prompted. Python discovery should resolve the interpreter
  via PATH (e.g. `which python3`, as Zed already does for other tooling) or
  accept an explicit interpreter path, so the managed Python is used and the
  CLT stub is never probed. Users who manage Python via Nix/uv/pyenv/etc.
  must be able to use Zed without installing or accepting Apple's Command
  Line Tools.
```

Multi-GB memory growth in basedpyright with `diagnosticMode` set to `"workspace"`

(apologies if this is a duplicate; I searched for related issues but couldn't find any with this exact situation, though I found others about unbounded memory growth)

### Reproduction steps

1. Add this block to your `settings.json`:
```json
{
  "lsp": {
    "basedpyright": {
      "settings": {
        "basedpyright.analysis": {
          "diagnosticMode": "workspace"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```
2. Open a repo with multiple Python files (mine has 80).
3. Restart the language server and wait 10 minutes.
4. Observe high memory usage by the language server process, growing over time.

In my case, it grew from ~400MB at initialization to nearly 3GB.

I wrote this issue text myself, but my LLM had a diagnosis that I thought sounded reasonable (and I verified the steps it took to test it):
<details>
<summary>LLM diagnosis</summary>

> My diagnosis is that Zed’s workspace-diagnostics timeout is creating a retry loop. Every two minutes, Zed cancels the existing request and starts a new one. Basedpyright treats each new request as a reason to analyze the workspace again, so memory grows with every retry.
>
> I tested this by temporarily preventing repeated requests from starting another analysis. Zed continued to time out and retry—eight times over 17 minutes—but basedpyright settled at about 19 MiB instead of growing toward 3 GiB. This suggests the repeated requests, rather than the project’s size, are causing the growth.
>
> I believe Zed should own the primary fix because it creates and controls the retry loop, and `diagnosticMode: "workspace"` is explicitly supported in Zed’s Python documentation. Basedpyright keeping the request open contributes to the interaction, but that behavior is inherited from Pyright. Zed can prevent the repeated work for both servers by handling a timed-out workspace-diagnostics request without immediately starting the same work again.
>
> For comparison, VS Code’s standard language client leaves the current workspace-diagnostics request open and processes partial results as they arrive. It only starts another request after the current one finishes and does not apply Zed’s 120-second inactivity timeout. This allows basedpyright’s long-running request to remain active without repeatedly restarting workspace analysis. This behavior is visible in [VS Code’s language-client implementation](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-languageserver-node/blob/main/client/src/common/diagnostic.ts#L481-L531).
</details>

### Current vs. Expected behavior

Current behaviour: Memory usage grows unboundedly in workspace mode.
Expected behaviour: Memory usage stays roughly flat over time after the initial workspace analysis.

Scope-based language settings are ignored when the cursor is at the end of the buffer ### Reproduction steps 1. Start Zed with default settings. 2. Create end-of-file.c and type // it (with a space after it). Don't press Enter, so the cursor is the last position in the buffer. 3. Type '. 4. For comparison, create middle-of-file.c with two lines, // it and int x;. Put the cursor at the end of line 1 and type '. ### Current vs. Expected behavior Current: at the end of the buffer, ' auto-closes to '' inside the comment (first screenshot). With a line after the comment, it stays a single ' (second screenshot). Expected: ' doesn't auto-close inside a comment anywhere in the file. Zed's C config says so: { start = "'", end = "'", close = true, newline = false, not_in = ["string", "comment"] }. Likely cause: in crates/language/src/buffer.rs, language_scope_at walks down from each layer's root node while child_range.contains(&offset). Range::contains excludes the end, so when offset equals the buffer length the root node doesn't contain the cursor. No layer matches, and the function falls back to the buffer's language with override_id: None. Every setting that depends on the override scope is then lost at the end of the buffer: brackets.not_in, [overrides.] line_comments, and anything else read through language_scope_at. Extensions hit it too. One language sets [overrides.preproc] line_comments = ["// "] so that Enter after #define X 1 inserts nothing. When that line is the last one in the buffer, Enter inserts # anyway. ### Zed version and system specs Zed: v1.21.0+stable.362.33c95853ed2b6956f339733c63a8220964ecbeb6 (Zed) OS: Linux X11 fedora 44 Memory: 46.7 GiB Architecture: x86_64 ### Attach Zed log file
